moc: Old St Paul's Cathedral: very long Gothic nave with a square crossing tower and NO spire (spire lost 1561), NO dome
Old London Bridge lined with houses
NO Wren dome or Wren steeples

ghi_chu.mo_ta: The men wear long knee-length buttoned coats (justaucorps style) with white linen cravats, and knee breeches with white stockings. Their wigs are full and long.
ghi_chu.ly_do: This looks like 1680s dress. In 1666 men wore short doublets or jackets with loose petticoat breeches and falling bands. The vest and coat fashion was only introduced by Charles II in October 1666. Full-bottomed wigs and lace cravats became common in the 1670s and 1680s.

ghi_chu.mo_ta: The window skyline shows low roofs and one small pointed spire, with a smoke column rising. There is no large Old St Paul's, with its long Gothic nave and square crossing tower, in the view.
ghi_chu.ly_do: If the view is toward the City, Old St Paul's should dominate the skyline as a massive Gothic church with a square tower. It appears to be absent or not identifiable. This finding is low confidence.
